hero.description: Use Wan 2.6 to generate high-quality images and videos from prompts or reference images—via web UI or API.

paragraphs: Wan 2.6 is a multimodal generative Wan 2.6 model family used for tasks like text-to-image creation and image-to-video generation.
In practice, it can transform prompts and reference images into production-ready visuals—supporting workflows from early concepting to marketing assets and iterative creative exploration.
joymagic provides an integration layer to run these workflows via a web UI and (when enabled) API access, so you can move from experimentation to automation with fewer steps.

creations.h2: What can you create with Wan 2.6?

t2i.p: Turn prompts into images for product concepts, illustrations, and marketing creatives. Experiment with styles, compositions, and aspect ratios without changing tools.

editing.p: Create variations, stylize references, and iterate through refinements. Use the same prompt framework to converge on a final look faster.

i2v.p: Animate a single image into a short video clip. Guide motion with a prompt, keep key elements consistent, and iterate with variations to dial in the exact feel you want.

For high-intent workflows like ads and product clips, Wan 2.6 image-to-video (or I2V) starts from an input image and generates a short sequence with motion guided by your prompt. You can tune output duration, pick an HD preset, and use a motion prompt to control movement—if your endpoint supports higher presets like 1080p, you’ll see it as an option.

inputs.p: Provide a reference image plus a prompt describing the scene and desired motion. Clear subjects and clean backgrounds generally improve stability.

controls.p: Adjust resolution presets and duration where available. Add motion language (camera moves, subject motion, ambience) to steer results in a repeatable way.

use_cases.p: Product videos, social ads, b-roll style motion, cinematic shots, and quick storyboards—especially when you need rapid iteration across many variants.

1.p: Pick text-to-image for stills, or image-to-video when you want motion from a reference image.

2.h3: 2. Add a prompt (and reference image if needed)
2.p: Describe the subject, style, and context. For I2V, add motion guidance like “slow push-in” or “subtle drifting smoke”.

3.h3: 3. Set output options (resolution, duration, aspect ratio)
3.p: Choose the output preset that matches your channel (social, web, ads). Keep options consistent for repeatable workflows.

4.p: Generate a first pass quickly, then review for subject consistency, motion quality, and composition.

5.p: Make small prompt changes and compare outputs. Save the best results as references for the next iteration.

6.p: Download assets for your pipeline or integrate generation via API for batch and automation use cases.

api.p: Build production integrations for Wan 2.6 API access using simple REST/JSON requests. Authentication is typically handled with an API key, and you can connect generation to your existing product workflow for batch runs, templates, and team tools.

items.question: What is Wan 2.6 used for?
items.answer: Wan 2.6 is used for multimodal generation workflows such as text-to-image and image-to-video. You can turn prompts into images, create variations and edits, or animate a reference image into a short clip. On joymagic, Wan 2.6 fits into end-to-end workflows for prototyping, marketing creatives, and production asset generation.

items.question: Is Wan 2.6 good for image-to-video?
items.answer: Wan 2.6 image-to-video (I2V) is a strong fit when you want to start from a still image and add controlled motion with a prompt. It’s commonly used for product shots, ad creatives, b-roll style clips, and concept visuals. Results depend on the reference image quality and how specific your motion prompt is.

items.question: How do I write prompts for Wan 2.6?
items.answer: Start with a clear subject, then add style, lighting, and camera details. For I2V, include a motion prompt that describes the movement (e.g., “slow push-in”, “subtle wind”, “camera pan left”) and what should stay stable. Iterate with small changes and keep a short “negative” list of things you want to avoid if your workflow supports it.

items.question: Does Wan 2.6 support 1080p output?
items.answer: Output resolution (including 1080p) depends on the specific endpoint and presets available in the UI or API at the time you generate. If 1080p is supported for your mode, you’ll see it as a selectable option; otherwise generate at the highest available preset and upscale downstream. Check the current presets on joymagic before standardizing a production workflow.

items.question: How much does Wan 2.6 cost?
items.answer: joymagic uses a credit-based pricing model. Typical starting points are from 2 credits per text-to-image generation and from 250 credits per image-to-video conversion, with totals varying by model, resolution, and duration. For up-to-date packs and plan details, see the pricing page—credit costs may change as features and providers evolve.

items.question: Can I use outputs commercially?
items.answer: Commercial use is generally allowed on joymagic, as long as you follow our Terms of Service and content policies. You’re responsible for ensuring you have the rights to any input images, logos, or brand assets you upload. If you need strict compliance requirements, review the Terms and policies linked on this page before launching.

items.question: Do you provide a Wan 2.6 API?
items.answer: Yes—joymagic offers API access for supported generation workflows so you can integrate Wan 2.6 into your product or pipeline. The API is typically REST/JSON and authenticated with an API key from your dashboard. For the latest endpoints, parameters, and examples, follow the API docs link on this page.
